transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood PM); Tom Reed (Helm Labs CTO), Anika Das (ML Eng), Marcus Lee (Platform), Juliette Marlow (PO)

Summary:
Redwood ran a product walkthrough focused on structured JSON output and function/tool calling in JSON mode. Customer is evaluating for a pilot to replace parts of their current K8s-hosted inference stack; key concerns are private deployment, schema enforcement, and how guardrails/Optimize recommendations reduce hallucinations and unit cost. Next steps: pilot pricing, sample schemas, benchmark scripts, and a private-deploy scoping session.

Topics covered:
- JSON mode + schema validation (live demo)
- Tool/function calling: DB lookup + internal vector store use-case
- Guardrails and structured output enforcement (Console + API examples)
- Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization/caching)
- Private deployment considerations (VPC, KMS, SOC2)

Action items (recap given at end of call):
- See action_items metadata above for owners/due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Singh: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Hi Tom, thanks for making time. We're gonna walk through JSON mode and a small tool-calling flow that'll map to the Helm Labs search + enrich pipeline.
[00:00:12] Tom Reed: Yeah thanks Maya, excited. Quick context: we're running in-house inference on k8s nodes, a mix of A100 and some rented instances, average p50 latency target is 200 ms for short queries, cost is obviously a thing.
[00:00:27] Carlos Ortega: got it. Quick qual q—what models are you currently running in prod for the search enrichment? Llama-2 variants? Mistral?
[00:00:34] Anika Das: Mostly Llama 2 13B and a custom fine-tune for reranking. We're testing Mistral for some lower-cost paths, but haven't moved it to prod.
[00:00:41] Marcus Lee: infra note: we need private control plane options and KMS integration — SOC2 stuff, yes.
[00:00:47] Maya Singh: Perfect, we'll cover Private later in the call. For the demo, Carlos will show Console and some API calls — schema enforcement and function/tool-calling.
[00:00:58] Carlos Ortega: Cool. I'm gonna share my screen — I might describe some things as the transcription catches up. Starting with the Redwood Console: this is the model route config for a "search-enrich-v1" endpoint. We have a JSON mode toggle here — when enabled, the runtime validates responses against a JSON Schema mmm — excuse me — a user provided schema and will reject or sanitize non-conforming output depending on the policy.
[00:01:26] Juliette Marlow: when you say reject, what does that look like? Do you get a 4xx from the API or do you receive a sanitized partial payload?
[00:01:34] Carlos Ortega: Good question. There are three modes: strict (API returns an error and logs), cleansing (runtime attempts to coerce into schema where safe and adds a warning meta field), and fallback where we call a smaller model variant to try again. You can set this per-route.
[00:01:50] Anika Das: That fallback option sounds useful — we currently see a lot of variance with structured outputs and it's killing downstream parsers.
[00:01:57] [00:02:10] Speaker 2: Mm hmm.
[00:02:12] Carlos Ortega: For tool calling, we wire functions in at the SDK layer: you declare the function signature in the schema, Redwood will surface a function call event in the stream and then your orchestrator (or Redwood's function runner) can execute the call and feed results back into the model context.
[00:02:29] Tom Reed: So like OpenAI function calling? Is the contract the same?
[00:02:33] Maya Singh: Similar idea, but with extra pieces for production: first, the function signatures can be validated against a JSON Schema; second, the Console has guardrail policies — for example, you can block outbound network calls from the function runner in pilot mode, or you can whitelist only certain internal services.
[00:02:50] Marcus Lee: we need that whitelisting. We're not ok with arbitrary outbound calls during tests.
[00:02:53] Carlos Ortega: Exactly — there's RBAC on which functions can be invoked, and we tie audit logs to user identities via our control plane.
[00:03:00] Anika Das: demo time?
[00:03:02] Carlos Ortega: Demo. Showing a sample prompt — the model is asked to return a structured JSON with fields: id, title, top_k_hits (array of up to 5 objects), each hit has score, source, snippet, and a vector_match field. I'm going to trigger the endpoint in JSON mode.
[00:03:24] [00:03:30] Carlos Ortega: Sending request now — watch the stream.
[00:03:34] [00:03:40] Carlos Ortega: Stream yields a function_call event: name=vector_query, args={"query":"<..>","k":5}. That gets handled by our runner, which hits a local vector store stub (in the demo environment) and returns the top results. Model then composes final JSON.
[00:03:57] Anika Das: I like that flow. How deterministic is the output? We need stable keys and array ordering for parsers downstream.
[00:04:05] Carlos Ortega: We enforce key sets via schema; array ordering is not strictly guaranteed unless you tee a sort key back in the schema and the model populates it. In practice we also provide a post-process step in the runner that can sort, dedupe, and normalize outputs.
[00:04:22] Juliette Marlow: Could you show the failure mode — like when the model returns a string instead of array?
[00:04:28] Carlos Ortega: Sure. Toggling to "strict" mode and re-sending same prompt…
[00:04:43] [00:04:50] Carlos Ortega: API returned 422 with validation error: expected top_k_hits to be array. Console shows the failed payload and a suggestion: either fix prompt or enable cleansing.
[00:04:58] Tom Reed: Helpful. On the cost side, you mentioned Optimize can suggest batching and quantization rules. Can you show that?
[00:05:07] Maya Singh: Priya, do you want to walk Optimize?
[00:05:10] Priya Patel: Sure — opening Redwood Optimize workspace. We ingest a sample workload (CSV of prompts + target latency) and the optimizer runs a quick analysis. For Helm's profile here (short queries, high qps) it suggests: enable continuous batching with max latency 250 ms, use 8-bit quantized weights for cheaper variants for non-critical routes, and enable prefix KV caching for repeated prefixes (looks like you have repeated preamble in your prompts). It also gives an estimated cost savings percentage and a predicted p95 latency with the suggested config.
[00:05:40] Marcus Lee: How accurate are those savings? If we commit to Dedicated, we need predictable unit cost.
[00:05:45] Priya Patel: The estimator uses archived run traces and kernel selection heuristics. It's an estimate — we back it with a dedicated benchmark script we can run on your infra to provide an SLA-backed projection for Dedicated.
[00:05:58] Tom Reed: Ok send us the benchmark script.
[00:06:01] Maya Singh: We'll include that as an action item.
[00:06:03] [00:06:10] Speaker 1: right
[00:06:12] Carlos Ortega: Back to guardrails — for hallucination mitigation we do several things: schema enforcement, few-shot examples in prompt templates injected server-side, and we support a rerank step where a safety model checks factual claims against an internal doc store. That rerank can be synchronous or async depending on latency needs.
[00:06:32] Anika Das: The rerank sounds like a must. Does it add a lot of latency?
[00:06:36] Carlos Ortega: If you run it sync with a heavy safety model, yes it adds overhead. Option: run a lightweight verifier first, then enqueue a stronger check async and mark the object as provisional. Many customers use provisional + audit logs.
[00:06:50] Juliette Marlow: For our product, provisional is fine for suggestions but not for final actions.
[00:06:55] Maya Singh: Makes sense. We'll map routes: suggestion vs final action.
[00:06:58] [00:07:10] Tom Reed: On privacy: Private deployment — do you have a private control plane that still gives us the Console but without control plane data leaving the VPC?
[00:07:18] Maya Singh: Yes — Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane that talks to a local agent. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key wrap and we ship audit logs to your SIEM. For SOC2 we provide the standard artifacts; we can schedule a security review with our compliance team.
[00:07:34] Marcus Lee: We'll need SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC.
[00:07:38] Carlos Ortega: Available. RBAC maps to roles and you can scope function invocation rights to roles.
[00:07:44] Anika Das: Quick question about latency: you support continuous KV cache for autoregressive workloads? We need warm cache behavior for multi-turn chat.
[00:07:53] Carlos Ortega: Yes — KV cache persists per request key for a configurable TTL, and the runtime can store per-customer cache shards. This reduces tokens per request when you have repeated contexts.
[00:08:04] [00:08:10] Juliette Marlow: If we want to run a pilot, what's the fastest path? Hosted or Dedicated?
[00:08:15] Maya Singh: For quick proof-of-concept, Hosted with a dedicated route and pilot quotas is fastest (you get Console + API in days). For predictable throughput and data isolation, Dedicated is next step. Private is for full VPC/on-prem needs. We typically recommend Hosted pilot with a view to commit to Dedicated if you need SLA and cost predictability.
[00:08:34] Tom Reed: I think pilot then Dedicated. We'll need pricing for Dedicated.
[00:08:38] Maya Singh: We'll include both hosted-pilot pricing and Dedicated commit options in the follow-up.
[00:08:42] [00:08:48] Carlos Ortega: demo continued — now I'm going to show a schema with nested objects and a pattern property for ISO timestamps. The Console allows you to paste or upload a JSON schema, then you can attach a policy: strict/cleansing/fallback and choose which function signatures are allowed.
[00:09:05] [00:09:20] Carlos Ortega: Triggering a sample that intentionally violates the ISO string in the timestamp field…
[00:09:25] [00:09:30] Carlos Ortega: Runtime flagged validation error; cleansing mode coerced timestamp into ISO and added a "__redwood_warn" field with a short message.
[00:09:39] Anika Das: That warn field — is that surfaced to the event store or hidden?
[00:09:44] Carlos Ortega: It's in the response body and we also log the event to the Console audit trail. You can set retention on those logs in the Console.
[00:09:52] Tom Reed: For compliance we want e2e logs but also easy purge.
[00:09:56] Maya Singh: You can set retention and export to your SIEM.
[00:10:00] [00:10:12] Speaker 2: okay
[00:10:14] Carlos Ortega: Now I want to show the API payload for function calling. Example: POST /v1/generate with body: {"mode":"json","schema":"<schema-id>","prompt":"...","tools":[{"name":"vector_query","sig":{...}}]} — you'll see the stream events include model tokens and function_call events. We also emit granular token-level latency and cost in the trace.
[00:10:39] Marcus Lee: token-level cost is great for chargeback. How do we get that into our billing?
[00:10:43] Priya Patel: The Console exposes per-token cost buckets and exportable CSV/BigQuery sink. Many customers plug that into chargeback dashboards.
[00:10:52] Tom Reed: Are you able to attach custom metrics? We have internal ops metrics we want correlated with Redwood traces.
[00:10:58] Maya Singh: Yep — you can add tracing hooks and push events to your tracing backend.
[00:11:02] [00:11:10] Anika Das: A technical deep dive question: when the model calls a function and we feed the DB results back into the prompt, are those tokens billable? We're trying to get clarity on what counts as tokens for billing.
[00:11:20] Carlos Ortega: Good nuance — tokens generated by the model are billable. Tool responses that are injected do not count as model-generated tokens, but if you then prompt the model with the tool-injected content and the model generates more, those generated tokens are billable. We surface a token breakdown in traces so you can see modeling vs tech-injected tokens.
[00:11:40] Tom Reed: Sounds fair.
[00:11:42] [00:11:50] Carlos Ortega: For more advanced guardrails we support a post-generation verifier that compares claims to a canonical doc store. The verifier returns a verdict and a confidence score; if confidence < threshold we mark result provisional. You can configure a policy to auto-reject or flag.
[00:12:07] Juliette Marlow: Can these policies be tested in a staging workspace?
[00:12:11] Maya Singh: Yes — you can create multiple workspaces with isolated configs and run traffic against them. We'll set up a Helm sandbox workspace for your pilot.
[00:12:19] Anika Das: One more question on schemas: does Redwood support custom formats beyond standard JSON Schema (like custom regex validators or cross-field constraints)?
[00:12:29] Carlos Ortega: We support JSON Schema draft and also allow you to register custom validators (lambda-like JS functions) that run in the sandboxed runner. Those custom validators can be scoped by role.
[00:12:41] Marcus Lee: Are those validators auditable? We need to show proof of validators used in production during audits.
[00:12:46] Priya Patel: Validators are versioned and logged; the Console shows the validator version and diff with last deployment.
[00:12:53] [00:13:00] Speaker 3: cool
[00:13:03] Carlos Ortega: Ok switching back to Optimize — I'm going to demo a quick simulated run where we import 10k sample queries. Watch the suggestion panel: shows batching (8-32 depending on latency SLO), quantization tier for each route, and expected p95. You can click "apply" to push configs to a route or export as a YAML to use in your infra-as-code.
[00:13:29] Anika Das: If we apply suggested quantization, do you support mixed-precision for finer control?
[00:13:34] Carlos Ortega: Yes, we expose per-layer quantization knobs for advanced use, but Optimize will give a safe default (e.g., q4_k_m for 13B-class models) and show quality regressions on a test prompt set.
[00:13:47] Tom Reed: Will you show a sample regression report?
[00:13:50] Carlos Ortega: Sure — opens report: shows a few prompts where ROUGE/EM decreased; we highlight which outputs are regressed and you can drill into token diffs.
[00:13:59] Juliette Marlow: How do regressions get baked into a decision? We need approval workflows.
[00:14:04] Maya Singh: Console supports rollout policies — you can create a canary with x% traffic and a guardrail that blocks rollout if quality metrics drop below threshold. That ties to our rollouts feature.
[00:14:14] Marcus Lee: Great.
[00:14:17] [00:14:30] Carlos Ortega: Now some real-world notes — when you use function calling with vector lookups, common pitfalls are: prompt context explosion (too many tokens), mismatch between vector store schema and model output, and naive sorting. We recommend: concise retrieval results, include only top-k with condensed snippets, and use a sorting key to enforce deterministic ordering.
[00:14:50] Anika Das: Implementation question: can the function runner be in our VPC, or does it need to be run by Redwood?
[00:14:56] Maya Singh: For Private you run the runner inside your VPC and we provide the agent. For Hosted we offer a managed runner but you can use a customer-hosted runner that calls back to our control plane — depends on your security posture.
[00:15:08] Tom Reed: About observability: we need traces, token-level latency, and model-level breakdowns per route.
[00:15:14] Priya Patel: Console traces include token-level timings, kernel selection, and the model variant used. You can export to your tracing backend with OpenTelemetry.
[00:15:24] [00:15:30] Carlos Ortega: Almost at half-time — quick checkpoint: any blockers for pilot?
[00:15:36] Tom Reed: Main things: cost estimate for Dedicated, SAML + RBAC + KMS details, and the benchmark script. Also want sample schema examples for our search-enrich use-case.
[00:15:44] Maya Singh: Good — those are in next_steps.
[00:15:47] [00:15:55] Speaker 1: okay
[00:15:58] Carlos Ortega: I'll switch to a short Q&A section in the demo.
[00:16:04] [00:16:10] Anika Das: One edge case — sometimes the model invents a source URL. Can you force the model to only return sources from the vector hits?
[00:16:17] Carlos Ortega: Yes — you can tie the schema to only allow certain enumerated source domains or use the verifier to cross-check that source is in the provided hits payload. With strict mode you'd reject if mismatch.
[00:16:30] Tom Reed: How does Redwood handle large result sets? We're used to returning top 50 for internal tools.
[00:16:36] Carlos Ortega: For large sets, we recommend streaming with pagination. The API supports streaming JSON arrays and emitting partial batches. That keeps p50 low and allows downstream to start processing.
[00:16:49] Marcus Lee: streaming is key for us.
[00:16:51] [00:16:58] Maya Singh: Quick note on contracts: if you commit to Dedicated, we typically do a 3–12 month reserved capacity with optional overage. We'll send two pricing scenarios.
[00:17:07] Tom Reed: We'll want both flat and percent-overage models.
[00:17:11] [00:17:20] Carlos Ortega: Demo wrap: I'm going to show a quick hands-on script that uses the SDK to declare a function and run an end-to-end call. (He pastes code snippet) sample request -> stream -> function_call -> runner -> final JSON.
[00:17:36] [00:17:44] Carlos Ortega: Small transcription glitch here: the code var name was vectorQuery vs vector_query — please note naming is exact in the SDK.
[00:17:52] Anika Das: Good catch.
[00:17:55] [00:18:05] Juliette Marlow: A question on governance — can we enforce that prod routes always run with strict schema and staging with cleansing?
[00:18:12] Maya Singh: Yes — route configs are environment-scoped and you can lock policies for prod routes.
[00:18:17] Tom Reed: last question, can Redwood help with prompt engineering and building the initial schema? We don't have schema authors on the team.
[00:18:25] Maya Singh: We offer services and onboarding to help build prompt templates and schemas — that's part of the pilot engagement.
[00:18:31] [00:18:38] Speaker 2: okay thanks
[00:18:40] Carlos Ortega: We're almost at the end — recap of follow-ups: send pricing, pilot SOW, sample schemas, benchmark scripts, schedule private-deploy scoping.
[00:18:51] Tom Reed: Sounds good. We'd like the sandbox workspace before the end of next week if possible.
[00:18:57] Maya Singh: We'll aim for that.
[00:19:00] [00:19:12] Juliette Marlow: Quick nit: logging retention — can we set shorter retention for non-prod?
[00:19:17] Priya Patel: Yes retention is configurable per workspace.
[00:19:20] [00:19:30] Carlos Ortega: Closing the demo — anyone wants a deeper technical session we can do a SE-led deep dive for infrastructure, or a CSM lane for onboarding.
[00:19:39] Tom Reed: Let's schedule infra deep dive with our platform team.
[00:19:44] Maya Singh: I'll send calendar invites.
[00:19:47] [00:20:00] Speaker 1: thanks
[00:20:03] Maya Singh: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and action items.
